(The voice preview path is exempt by the technique's own rule: it speaks a fixed sentence authored for the ear, voiceEngineShared.tsx:323.)

The technique's 'when not to apply' clause governs: the dictated transcript's destination is the companion's language model, which holds the whole thread, so a small normalizer in between would be a lossy edit by the less-informed party. The stage is correctly absent.

pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/engine/src/prompt/assemble.rs:855 returns a bare String with no budget and no seal — assemble.rs:810-812 states there is no prompt-level budget by design, and a caller appends the memory layer after the door closes (src-tauri/src/commands/execution/executions.rs:547), so memory rides outside the budget, the trust classifier and the fingerprint.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/engine/src/prompt/assemble.rs:93 is a genuine single assembler with owned sections, but the stability gradient is broken in both directions: per-call sections render above the standing layers (render_correction_required at assemble.rs:159 and '## Triggering Event' at assemble.rs:165 precede '## Identity'/'## Instructions' at assemble.rs:214-231), so no byte-stable prefix survives; and the door does not seal — the returned String is appended to by prepared_run_cache::append_memories at src-tauri/src/commands/execution/executions.rs:547, after '## EXECUTE NOW'.

src-tauri/engine/src/prompt/variables.rs:18 reads chrono::Utc::now() inside the rendering pass, so assembly is not a pure function of declared inputs and no fingerprint over it can be stable; and variables.rs:122 renders an unresolved placeholder as literal {{key}} text the model reads as scaffolding — one of the two outcomes the technique names as dishonest, with the warn at variables.rs:128 reaching only the operator. Trust classification is otherwise correct (trusted magic vars vs sanitized input_data at variables.rs:21/85) and the announced truncation at runtime_safety.rs:180-185 is a model realization of naming what was dropped.

No owned vocabulary section with one authority exists; the project's terms are scattered across constant blobs the assembler pushes (templates.rs:13 MEMORY_SYSTEM_PREAMBLE, assemble.rs:613 'Personas Tool Semantics'), so a term's definition can be sharpened in one blob and not the other, and there is no single file the assembler renders.

No feeder declares whether what it contributes is reachable or unreachable — every section between assemble.rs:379 and assemble.rs:698 is pushed unconditionally with no class attached — so nothing marks which material may be cut first, and the material the provider's tail truncation reaches first is the task itself (assemble.rs:813-829).

src-tauri/engine/src/prompt/assemble.rs:810-812 states outright that there is no prompt-level byte budget, and assemble.rs:813-821 dumps the entire input_data JSON uncapped: no floors, no elastic allowances, no per-section ladder and no per-section token accounting, so the provider's silent tail truncation is the de-facto degradation policy. (The per-variable cap with its announced marker at runtime_safety.rs:98-185 is the one rung done well.)

The message list is owned by the Claude Code CLI, not by this assembler — cli_args.rs:101-112 pipes one prompt on stdin and cli_args.rs:288-298 resumes by session id — so the pairing invariant, the dangling-call repair and both compaction paths have no surface here.

The tool and capability layers are correctly derived (capabilities.rs:367 build_tool_documentation over the registered tools, capabilities.rs:108 render_active_capabilities filtered to enabled use cases), but the protocol-tool roster is hand-written prose at assemble.rs:403-424, restated a second time at templates.rs:272 (PROTOCOL_INTEGRATION_REQUIREMENTS) and a third time as a dead constant at templates.rs:130, whose own comment records that it 'was never wired into any prompt assembly'. Three copies of one vocabulary with no sync check against engine::dispatch is the drift the technique exists to prevent.

capabilities.rs:203-224 stamps a session-pool key from the enabled capability set, which is the right gate, but the digest is a join of id@title only — not the template version, not the persona's identity/instructions text, not the model family. A capability whose body was rewritten hashes identical, so a pooled warm session keeps running the prompt it was born with; this is the technique's 'digest identities, not summaries that collide' caution realized.

The prompt leaves as one stdin blob to the Claude CLI (cli_args.rs:101-103) and caching is delegated to it by environment (cli_args.rs:174-199 PROMPT_CACHE_POLICY and the DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING removals); there are no caller-declared cut points to allocate, which is this technique's stated precondition.

resume_prompt.rs:9 is a correct delta prompt for the preserved-session regime — it re-derives the volatile ground (credential hints, connector hints) rather than replaying — but nothing compares a stamped fingerprint before continuing: resume_prompt.rs:16 opens with 'Continue the previous execution.' and cli_args.rs:285 attaches --resume unconditionally, so a session opened before a capability or persona edit continues under rules that no longer exist in the source.

assemble.rs:826-829 opens the task layer with 'You are {name}. Execute your task now.' — a competence re-assertion in the primacy position of every call, which the measured record prices at nothing. Done is present and machine-checkable (the required protocol lines, assemble.rs:837-841); Locate is absent (no pointer to where the task's material lives) and Check exists only in DELIBERATE mode (templates.rs:234), so the default AUTONOMOUS path ships no verification step.

pairs.evidence: vitest.config.ts:17 includes src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx} with no exclude, so the e2e suite's own files (src/test/e2e/cli-*.e2e.test.ts, declared at vitest.e2e.config.ts:15) are also discovered by the default unit run — the partition is not disjoint and `npm test` runs them at the unit tier's budget.

techniques.evidence: The portfolio is real and legible — five vitest configs plus playwright, membership by location — but the default suite's discovery boundary is not explicit: vitest.config.ts:17 matches every src/**/*.test.ts, which includes the e2e lane's src/test/e2e/cli-*.e2e.test.ts (vitest.e2e.config.ts:15). Each file must be matched by exactly one configuration; here two configurations claim the same files with different environments and budgets. Separately, vitest.integration.config.ts:14 points at src/test/integration/rounds/, which does not exist on disk, so that lane certifies nothing while appearing to exist.

The precondition is a suite split across parallel workers whose assignment can be made duration-aware; the unit lane declares no sharding and no retained timing history (vitest.config.ts carries no pool/shard configuration), so there is no allocation for this technique to correct.

These tests sit at the cheapest fixture rung the technique prescribes for unit tier — in-memory construction, no environment build: the scan() factory at src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/__tests__/sceneStore.test.ts:7, the shared __tests__/passportFactory.ts builder, and a per-test reset of the module singleton at __tests__/persistence.test.ts:17 (__resetLayoutStoreForTests). No shared mutable fixture and no per-test rebuild.

Every claim in this context is a pure-logic derivation (deriveScene.*, tidyLayout, hex geometry) that nothing cheaper than a unit test could witness more cheaply; the repo carries its live lane elsewhere (playwright.config.ts, `test:smoke`), so this context correctly has no business on that rung.

Parallelism and environment are per-suite policy, not per-test discovery: vitest.config.ts:11 fixes jsdom for this lane while vitest.integration.config.ts:12/18 and vitest.cli.config.ts:9/13 declare node + forks for theirs; the lane inherits nothing from the developer's machine because the Tauri IPC surface is stubbed in the lane's own setup (src/test/setup.ts:5-13), and the one module singleton in this context is reset between tests (persistence.test.ts:17).

The precondition is a class of failure firing before the first test runs; a jsdom vitest lane over TypeScript sources in this repo has no such loader/manifest/architecture failure mode, and the quirks this project does absorb live in its Rust runner (scripts/build/run-rust-tests.mjs), outside this context.

stage: team precondition fails for this repo, and the technique's own stated prerequisite is absent with it: there is no retained, stably-keyed cross-run result history for this suite to detect outcome transitions from, and no quarantine register. Worth recording that no retry is configured either (vitest.config.ts declares none), so the suite at least does not mask flakes.
No endurance, load or chaos lane governs this context; these files run in seconds at the commit tier and judge boolean assertions, not statistical criteria.

The technique's own 'when not to use it' clause governs the bulk of this context: these are pure-logic assertions over derivation functions that go red on ordinary mistakes during development, so a ceremonial control adds nothing. One assertion would earn one — sceneStore.test.ts:78 asserts a concurrency ceiling (peak <= 4) that passes vacuously if the mapper ran serially or not at all — and no test in the context records the mutation that proved it can fail.

This context ships no artifact outside a gated root — the mastermind feature lives entirely under src/, which the default suite's declared membership reaches; the technique's population question (a shipped artifact no gated root builds) has no instance here.

pairs.subject: sync-replication
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/cloud/sync/mod.rs:407 propagates persona deletes from a tombstone table that nothing ever writes — grep over the workspace finds only the DDL (db/src/migrations/incremental/e06_teams_and_sync.rs:239) and the reader (rows.rs:907) — so a locally deleted persona lives in the cloud forever while the machinery reads as shipped.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/cloud/sync/mod.rs:58-75 is the per-stream declaration the engine is generic over — the pass, the cursor keys, the backfill policy and the status grid all derive from SYNC_TABLES, and mod.rs:593-606 guards its length and cursor-key uniqueness in a test. Direction and authority are declared once at mod.rs:1-15 (desktop projects up; the replica is RLS-scoped and never writes back in these paths).

The loop realizes most of the technique exactly — durable per-stream cursors (cursor.rs:33-51), the tick + lossy wake + persistent dirty mark triad (mod.rs:36-44, 498-531), advance-to-observed-max with the clock-capture race named in the comment (mod.rs:294-304), and error kept distinct from nothing-to-do (mod.rs:238-251, 484-486). Two rules fail: the watermark column is created_at with a 24-hour re-read window standing in for in-place mutations (mod.rs:56-57, 277-281), which the technique calls a stopgap with a measured margin — an execution or review updated more than a day after creation never reaches the cloud; and the first run is not chunked-and-resumable (mod.rs:287-305 reads the whole epoch backlog in one pass and advances the cursor only after every chunk settles, so an interrupted backfill restarts from zero).

The consumer side is complete and correct — table plus index at src-tauri/db/src/migrations/incremental/e06_teams_and_sync.rs:239, reader at rows.rs:907, cascade propagator with its own cursor at mod.rs:388-442 — and there is no producer: no code path in the workspace inserts into persona_tombstones, so no delete has ever propagated. This is the technique's named field defect ('name the line that writes the tombstone') verbatim. Two further gaps: the tombstone cursor advances to a wall clock captured before the read (mod.rs:409 and :436), the exact race the sibling cursor fixed 130 lines earlier; and only personas carry tombstones, so the other ten streams' deletes never transfer and the replica accretes rows forever.

Where a second device signs into the same account — which the design provides for (cursor.rs:110 mints a per-device id and mod.rs:315 heartbeats it into synced_devices) — two spokes write the same primary keys through client.rs:77's `resolution=merge-duplicates` upsert with no version, base hash or read-back, so resolution is last-arrival-wins: a race decided by network timing, whose loser is never told and which is declared nowhere. SYNC_TABLES (mod.rs:58) carries no conflict-policy column to declare it in.

Both halves are realized. Outbound is an allowlist built at one door per stream — the SELECTs enumerate columns and structurally never read the encrypted or vault classes (rows.rs:1-16) — with a payload projection that redacts by key needle and by value shape and bounds its size (rows.rs:36-80), and the projected key set is asserted in tests (rows.rs:926-944). Inbound scope is derived from the authenticated channel rather than the payload: user_id is deliberately absent from every row so Supabase defaults it from auth.uid() under RLS (rows.rs:14-16).

Most of the snapshot is there — per-table rows/error/cursor watermark with 'never synced' distinct from a placeholder (mod.rs:98-108, cursor.rs:56-62), fault isolation that lets the pass continue past a failed table (mod.rs:238-251), and last-success advanced only on a clean pass (mod.rs:484-486). What is missing is the pair that makes a cursor mean anything: TableSyncStatus (mod.rs:98-108) carries no source tail and no pending count, so a stalled stream whose local rows are piling up is indistinguishable from a healthy idle one, and the published `syncing` flag (mod.rs:117) is lifecycle state sitting beside health state.

pairs.registryProposal: Upward proposal for topology-declaration: its three shapes (one-way mirror, hub and spoke, peer merge) do not name the shape this repo is actually in — N spokes belonging to one principal, converging on a hub that orders nothing (a PostgREST upsert). It reads as a one-way mirror per device and behaves as a hub with no adjudication, which is why the conflict policy went undeclared here. The technique could name that fourth case and route it to conflict-detection's in-scope last-writer-wins lane (same mind at several keyboards), with the demand that the spoke's write carry what it believed was current.
